Win Condition 1: Big Bois: Big Mana Threats Cheated in from Rakdos
Win Condition 2: Group Slug: Damage Everyone Spells + Pingers
Win Condition 3: Half Doubled: Hidetsugu + Damage Doubler + Platinum Angel
Strength 1: Only need a few large bodies to take control of the game.
Strength 2: Enablers for Rakdos also serve as an alternative win condition by putting pressure on life totals.
Strength 3: Damage based card draw sources keep hand full of gas to fill board with Rakdos reduction.
Weakness 1: There is a heavy reliance on Rakdos to play large impact creatures due to their high CMC.
Weakness 2: The "life lost" casting requirement for Rakdos can make him difficult to cast consistently.
Weakness 3: Overextending and emptying your hand is easy to do, making board wipes or draw prevention painful.

Win Condition 1: Pillow Fort: Courts + Combat Taxes + Board Wipes
Win Condition 2: Goading & Bribery: Forced Combat & Political Incentives
Win Condition 3: Akaido: Combat Tricks & Fogs for Large Blowouts
Strength 1: Only requires a few permanents to shut down most combat damage and slow the game down.
Strength 2: Political mechanics like goad and monarchy allow for board manipulation, as well as conditional protection and value.
Strength 3: Versatile instant speed interactions that can swing the game in your favor.
Weakness 1: Dependant on mana rocks for most of the ramp package makes it vulnerable to artifact hate.
Weakness 2: Easy to become archenemy once pillow fort and value engines are up.
Weakness 3: Win conditions can be slow, leaving time for opponents to regain the upper hand.

Win Condition 1: Ping the Table: Artifact/Token Pingers + Treasures
Win Condition 2: Gold Hoard: Revel in Riches + Lots of Treasure
Win Condition 3: Stolen Spells: Cheat & Duplicate Stolen Exiled Spells
Strength 1: Exile/steal synergies help give card advantage while also having value payoffs.
Strength 2: Artifact/token/exile damage gets around clogged boards.
Strength 3: Treasures make up for Rakdos colors' weaker ramp options.
Weakness 1: Much slower if Prosper is shutdown since he's the primary value engine.
Weakness 2: Low power/non-combat focused creatures can struggle against focused attack from aggro/voltron.
Weakness 3: Impulse draw/stolen cards can lead to exiling a valuable but unplayable card.

Deck Representative(s): Miara, Thorn of the Glade & Kamahl, Heart of Krosa
Win Condition 1: Craterhoof Elf Ball: Kamahl + Elf Army
Win Condition 2: Drain the Table: Lathril + Elf Army + Copperhorn Scout (optional)
Win Condition 3: Ping the Table: Pingers + Elf Army + Sac Outlet or Board Wipe
Strength 1: Elf synergies, Miara draw on deaths, and token generation keeps up elfball tempo.
Strength 2: Kahmal makes the overrun win condition easily accessible.
Strength 3: No artifacts in the deck allows for one-sided artifact hate.
Weakness 1: Low budget of the deck means weaker/overcosted effects and an overall lower power.
Weakness 2: Kamahl in the command zone telegraphs main win condition.
Weakness 3: Reliance on critical mass of elves struggles with control and board wipe strategies.

Win Condition 1: Life Swap Shennanigans: Health Payment + Repay in Kind
Win Condition 2: Life Drain: Peer Into Abyss + Skirge + Exsanguinate
Win Condition 3: Health Storm Bomb: Bolas's Citadel and K'rrik + Blood Celebrant + Aetherflux Reservoir
Strength 1: Card draw is easy to pull off even without Vilis.
Strength 2: Life gain/loss manipulation and big swing spells gets around crowded board states.
Strength 3: Mana doublers and life payment allow for multi spell turns.
Weakness 1: Flatter curve can lead to clunky hands.
Weakness 2: 8 CMC commander is hard to cast, and is a target for removal given the cost and value potential.
Weakness 3: Lifegain strategy in mono-black is weaker compared to a deck with white.

Win Condition 1: Craterhoof Goat Swing: Ibex / Bogbeast + Any creatures + Wulfgar (optional)
Win Condition 2: Burn the Table: On Attack Burn All Players
Win Condition 3: Commander Damage: Wulfgar + Two-Handed Axe (Minimum 24 damage on attack)
Strength 1: Almost all creatures and permanents have on attack triggers to maximize value.
Strength 2: Large creatures, token generators, pump effects, trample and haste helps overrun boards.
Strength 3: Extra combat synergies with multiple on attack triggers.
Weakness 1: High CMC creatures can be difficult to cast if missing ramp or cheat effects.
Weakness 2: Less removal can lead to opponents running away with game or shutting down strategy.
Weakness 3: The "on attack" tribal strategy requires putting creatures in danger and leaving you open to crackbacks.

Decks: Nalia, Bring your +1 to the Party
Win Condition 1: One Sided Board Wipe: Stick Together & Damning Verdict
Win Condition 2: +1 Overrun: Cathar's Crusade + Tokens
Win Condition 3: Pump the Board: +X/+X effects
Strength 1: Synergies with +1/+1 counters can lead to snowballing effects.
Strength 2: Nalia can play all creatures off the top of the deck.
Strength 3: Low CMC creatures and token generators helps fill party quickly.
Weakness 1: Reliant on combat damage, so is weaker to pillow fort and stax strategies.
Weakness 2: Party mechanic has subpar payoffs, heavy creature investment, and limited synergies in Orzhov.
Weakness 3: This is a budget, upgraded precon.

Win Condition 1: Zombie Apocalypse: Gisa + Cheap Fatties + Zombie Lords & Tribal Anthems
Win Condition 2: Drain the Table: Pingers + Zombie tokens entering and leaving
Win Condition 3: Rise from the Graves: Mass Recursion + Full Graveyard
Strength 1: Zombie synergy and Gisa's ability can fill the board with zombies quickly.
Strength 2: Zombie enter/death triggers can deal damage to the table without relying on a big swing.
Strength 3: Several conditional tutors that can find combo pieces to close out games.
Weakness 1: Mono-black zombies misses strong tribal support from dimir and esper colors.
Weakness 2: Gisa is slow (5 to cast, 1 + tap to activate, creature to sac) and not a zombie.
Weakness 3: Graveyard hate can disrupt synergies with reanimation effects.

Win Condition 1: Fatties Swing: Cheat Big Creatures + Haste/Double Strike
Win Condition 2: Permanent Sacrifice Ping: Mayhem Devil and Stalking Vengeance
Win Condition 3: No Permanents 4 U: Vaevictus Targeted Sacrifice
Strength 1: Vaevictis is powerful spot removal on a stick.
Strength 2: All permanent focus means that you never a miss on commander's flip ability.
Strength 3: Redundant cheating permanents effects if commander is shut down.
Weakness 1: All permanents constraint leads to limited, sub-optimal ramp, card draw and interaction.
Weakness 2: High CMC creatures leads to clunky hands if cheat effects are shutdown.
Weakness 3: Higher cost commander that will attract removal.

Win Condition 1: Commander Damage: Tuvasa + Auras
Win Condition 2: Go Wide Value: Token Generators off of Enchantments Entering / Casts
Win Condition 3: Secret Commander: Bruna Cheating Auras
Strength 1: Synergies with enchantments give card draw, token generation, life gain and cost reduction.
Strength 2: Hidden commander, recusrion and draw engines make up for aura weaknesses.
Strength 3: No artifacts in the deck allows for one-sided artifact hate and stax.
Weakness 1: Enchantment hate will hit almost all permanents.
Weakness 2: Minimal instant speed interaction makes answering threats slower.
Weakness 3: Auras stacked on a single creature can lead to large blowouts from spot removal.

Win Condition 1: From the Grave: Loot and Reanimate Big Threats Early
Win Condition 2: Mass Reanimation: Living Death, Sepulchral, Twilight's Call
Win Condition 3: Board Control: Sacrifice/Tap effects for Large Swings
Strength 1: Vohar is low mana, though not integral to it working, and looting effects fill graveyard while filtering hands.
Strength 2: Looting and milling is redundant across reanimation effects, ensuring graveyard should always have a target.
Strength 3: Can get high threat creatures on board as early as turn 3.
Weakness 1: Graveyard hate will disrupt the primary strategy, and slow it down to hard casting large creatures.
Weakness 2: Most creatures are at 5+ CMC, making them hard to cast without reanimation.
Weakness 3: High threat creatures can make you archenemy, making you vulnerable to focused removal and wide boards.

Decks: A Refined Grizzly of Noble Heritage
Win Condition 1: Voltron Commander Damage: Wilson + Counters + One Sided Wipes
Win Condition 2: Backup Commander: Other Creature + Counters
Win Condition 3: Pillow Fort: Noble Heritage + Nils + Politics Cards
Strength 1: Wilson and Noble Heritage come down fast, can threaten knockouts by turn 5.
Strength 2: Instant speed combat tricks, protection and doublers allow for big swings.
Strength 3: Cheap cost and strong keywords on commander allow for redeployment at low costs.
Weakness 1: Voltron strategy is fragile if focused down by table.
Weakness 2: Counter strategy has less permamence on board than equipment strategies.
Weakness 3: Politics of deck fall apart if players decide not to engage when you're a threat.

Win Condition 1: Cascade Snowball: Cheat Large Threats via Cascade Triggers
Win Condition 2: Creature Overrun: Avenger Zendikar / Baloths + End Raze Forerunners
Win Condition 3: Burn it Down: Locus of Rage / Warstorm Surge
Strength 1: Averna is a strong engine that helps enable the strategy of the deck without being overly reliant on her.
Strength 2: Cascade enablers cheat threats onto the board and maintain tempo.
Strength 3: Strong land based ramp and landfall package can lead to fast snowballing.
Weakness 1: Cascade is high variance, which can lead to low impact flips and inconsistent turns.
Weakness 2: Creature and token focus leaves deck vulnerable to sweepers.
Weakness 3: Reliance on big spells means a slow start or early disruption can leave it vulnerable before it hits critical mass.

Win Condition 1: Voltron Commander Damage: Syr Gwyn + Piles of Equipment
Win Condition 2: Backup Commander(s): Both Danitha's or Fiendslayer or Akiri or Balan
Win Condition 3: Instant Speed Win Button: Akroma's Will + A Modestly Threatening Board
Strength 1: Gwyn has built in evasion, card draw, and cheats costs of most powerful equipment.
Strength 2: Other creatures synergize with same strategy as Gwyn, gives resiliency to normally fragile voltron.
Strength 3: Equipment tutors helps find the answer to specific problems or finishers.
Weakness 1: Gwyn is expensive at 6, without haste, requires protection, and is in colors that don't ramp out fast.
Weakness 2: Heavy reliance on equipment leaves deck vulnerable to artifact hate.
Weakness 3: Reputation of lethality can lead to targeting it down before it gets pieces on board.

Win Condition 1: Smash Your Face: Angels Protec and Attac
Win Condition 2: Big Bombs Every Turn: Seedborn + Mayael
Win Condition 3: Double Striking Lifelinkers: True Conviction + Any Number of Attackers
Strength 1: Angels are inherently big, scary creatures, a single one can win in right conditions.
Strength 2: Mayael's ability gets around biggest weaknesses of slow card advantage and high curve.
Strength 3: Protection from angels' abilities and less reliance on commander gives resiliency.
Weakness 1: High mana creatures can lead to clunky hands if you fall behind on mana.
Weakness 2: Less explosive and consistent card draw can lead to fizzling out in some instances.
Weakness 3: Heavy reliance on creatures and permanents means a board wipe can cripple an entire game.

Win Condition 1: Mass Reanimation Bombs: Nethroi Mutate / Eerie + Graveyard + Death Triggers (Optional)
Win Condition 2: Graveyard Loops: Reveillark, Karmic Guide, Victimize, Unburial Rites
Win Condition 3: Wipes: All Wipes One Sided With Graveyard Reanimation
Strength 1: Can fill up graveyard fast, enabling reanimation value and Nethroi triggers later on.
Strength 2: Multiple ETB and death triggers give sacrifice and reanimation a flexible toolbox.
Strength 3: Resilient from wipes and removal since it revolves around recursion.
Weakness 1: Graveyard hate cripples the gameplan and primary wincons.
Weakness 2: Setup dependent since it requires a full graveyard and the right reanimation window, leading to stalls.
Weakness 3: Mutate ability can be interrupted with instant speed removal, blowing up turns and causing tempo loss.

Win Condition 1: Drain the Table: Aristocrat Drain + Tokens + Sac Outlet
Win Condition 2: Clue Control: Clue Engines + Junk Winder
Win Condition 3: Sacrifice Loops: Several 4+ Card Sacrifice Combos can Fill the Board
Strength 1: Eloise ties strategy together where death triggers investigate, sacrifice clues lets you filter.
Strength 2: Token producers, sac outlets, recursion and payoffs give flexible strategies of control, value and combo.
Strength 3: Low curve enables easy rebuilds after wipes.
Weakness 1: Graveyard and artifact hate can heavily disrupt clue, recursion and death triggers.
Weakness 2: Setup intensive game plan requires multiple pieces on board before it can pressure the table.
Weakness 3: Reliant on aristocrat loops for wins, since creatures are small, leaving it vulnerable to big beaters and aggro.

Win Condition 1: Pirate Aggro: Pirate Army Attacks + Anthem
Win Condition 2: Gold Hoard: Revel in Riches + Lots of Treasure
Win Condition 3: Boarding Party: Steal Opponents Creatures
Strength 1: Aggression from wide board of pirate attacks and theft abilities disrupts opponents' boards.
Strength 2: Treasures provide ramp and color fixing, and can help rebuild from board wipes.
Strength 3: Pirates directly benefit from supporting one another, which are boosted by kindred payoffs.
Weakness 1: Pirates are a relatively weaker and less developed tribe.
Weakness 2: Theft ability of Brass requires a developed board, and can be hard to punch through with weaker creatures.
Weakness 3: Without anthems or combat tricks, pirate aggro can stall out against larger creatures or wide board states.

Win Condition 1: Clone Army: Orvar + Cheap Spells + Evasive/Card Draw Creatures
Win Condition 2: Flicker Combo: Ghostly Flicker + Peregrine Drake + Spell Recovery Mage
Win Condition 3: Token Swarm: Talrand / Murmuring Mystic / Master of Waves + Spellslinging
Strength 1: Orvar turns 1 mana cantrips into clone spells, bringing massive tempo and board threats.
Strength 2: Spellslinger momentum carries with card draw, token generation and clone effects.
Strength 3: Flexibile disruption suite offers interaction and defense while synergizing with the key strategies.
Weakness 1: Orvar dependent, if removed the spellslinger pieces are much lower impact since they lose the multiplicative clones.
Weakness 2: Combos are also Orvar dependent, so targeted removal can fizzle combo lines.
Weakness 3: Small creatures and engine setup means that the deck can be pressured early with aggro and large beaters.

Win Condition 1: Overrun Dinos: Cheat Dinosaurs into Play with Gishath
Win Condition 2: Dinosaur Aggro: Cost Reducers + Large Dino Threats
Win Condition 3: Value Burn: Warstorm Surge + Quartzwood Crasher
Strength 1: Dinosaurs have strong synergies, with top end power and triggers that outsize most other creature types.
Strength 2: Gishath's ability can quickly run away with the game if not answered.
Strength 3: Deep ramp package rolls into big dinosaurs ahead of curve.
Weakness 1: Gishath is slow and expensive, and if it is killed or blocked the deck loses its strongest momentum engine.
Weakness 2: Most value comes from dinosaurs sticking to the board, so board wipes can lead to a slow rebuild.
Weakness 3: Top heavy curve can have slow starts and no viable plays if you miss land drops or ramp.

Win Condition 1: Top Deck Group Slug: Yuriko + Big Mana + Topdeck Manipulation (optional)
Win Condition 2: Ninjas: Ninjitsu Abilities to Swing Game
Win Condition 3: Sneaky Bois: Small Evasive Creatures to Chip in Unblockable Damage
Strength 1: Yuriko is a persistent threat that can cheat commander tax, deal 10+ damage a turn, and net card advantage.
Strength 2: Top deck manipulation helps hit on Yuriko's ability and smooths out draws.
Strength 3: Life loss from Yuriko and unblockable creatures get around crowded board states.
Weakness 1: Yuriko's abilities leads to table focusing down commander, limits political leverage.
Weakness 2: If Yuriko is locked down, then deck can struggle to close out the game.
Weakness 3: Creatures are generally weaker, can be overrun by larger boards in the late game.

Deck Description: An Army of Cats and Dogs
Win Condition 1: Go Wide: Rin and Seri + Playing Creatures
Win Condition 2: Buff Cats and Dogs: Anthems & Overrun Effects
Win Condition 3: ETB Triggers: Impact Tremors & Felidar Retreat
Strength 1: Rin and Seri are an efficient passive token engine that rewards you for playing the deck.
Strength 2: Tribal synergies with anthems and buffs turn small creatures into lethal beaters.
Strength 3: Mid and late game scaling with token doublers and explosive draw rewards large boards.
Weakness 1: Leans heavily on wide board states, making it vulnerable to sweepers.
Weakness 2: Fog effects and pillow fort strategies shut down primary attack based wincons.
Weakness 3: Shutting down anthems weakens tiny tokens and can lead to blowouts.
